candidates.summary: In the vertical move, skip the check_for_hostile_collision call when check_for_mover_collision_with_movers found no collision (C = 0): the call only does LDA/LDY and returns C = 0; load Y = mover_to_update directly and branch to no_collision.
candidates.equivalence: Original no-collision path (C=0 from check_for_mover_collision_with_movers): JSR check_for_hostile_collision does LDA movers_type_and_colour,X (A, N, Z clobbered), LDY mover_to_update, BCC leave_with_carry_clear_242d -> RTS with C=0, Y=mover_to_update; then BCS not taken, falls into no_collision, which reloads X and A from tables indexed by Y and overwrites N/Z/A/X. New: LDY mover_to_update (C untouched), BCC taken straight to no_collision with the same Y, C=0, same memory. Nothing else is written on that path (hit_type and hostile_mover are only stored on the C=1 hostile path). Collision path (C=1): LDY is harmless (hostile loads Y itself from mover_to_update), BCC not taken, JSR/BCS identical to before, so hostile/not-hostile results, hit_type, hostile_mover and the vertical_collision_b245f path are unchanged. move_mover_up falls in and move_mover_down JSRs here; both get the same exits and the RTS from no_collision/vertical_collision is unchanged. Collision path costs 2 cycles more (BCC not taken) and is rare. no_collision label is referenced only here (grep).
